Professor Brian Cox visits some of the most stunning locations on earth to describe how the laws of nature have carved natural wonders across the solar system. Brian reveals how beauty and order in earth's cosmic backyard was formed from nothing more than a chaotic cloud of gas. Chasing tornados in Oklahoma, he explains how the same physics that creates these spinning storms shaped the young solar system. Out of this celestial maelstrom emerged the jewel in the crown, Brian's second wonder - the rings of Saturn. On an ice-choked lagoon in Iceland, he sees the nearest thing on earth to Saturn's rings. Using the latest scientific imagery and breathtaking graphics, he explains how the intricate patterns round Saturn are shaped by the cluster of more than 60 moons surrounding the planet. One of those moons makes a spectacular contribution to the rings and is the third wonder of the solar system. Brian describes the discovery of giant fountains of ice erupting from the surface of Enceladus

Professor Brian Cox describes how the laws of nature have carved natural wonders across the solar system. Brian reveals how something as flimsy as an envelope of gas - an atmosphere - can create some of the most wondrous sights. He takes a ride in an English Electric Lightning and flies 18 km up to the top of Earth's atmosphere, where he sees the darkness of space above and the thin blue line of our atmosphere below. In the Namib desert in south-west Africa, he tells the story of Mercury. This tiny planet was stripped naked of its early atmosphere and is fully exposed to the ferocity of space. Against the backdrop of Alaskan glaciers, Brian reveals his fourth wonder - Saturn's moon Titan, shrouded by a murky, thick atmosphere. He reveals that below the clouds lies a magical world. Titan is the only place beyond Earth where liquid pooling has been found on the surface in vast lakes as big as the Caspian Sea, but they are filled with a mysterious liquid and are unlike anything on Earth

As deep winter sets in, four Alaskans living in the remote bush must gather and manage scarce resources to ensure their survival. In isolated Kavik, Sue Aikens faces a life-and-death challenge when she returns to camp to find that thieves have pilfered her winter fuel supply. Meanwhile in Noorvik, Chip and Agnes Hailstone are unable to access their hunting grounds and must hope for local trapping and trading to survive. In Eagle, Andy Bassich and his wife Kate face a crisis with their team of malamutes, who they depend upon completely in order to survive the wilderness. And in Wiseman, Erik Salitan sets out to catch dinner but returns home with more than he bargained for.

p.t: Ben Fogle: New Lives in the Wild
p.d: Ben travels to the canyons of Utah to meet 72-year-old twins Bill and Bob Stone, who fled their adrenaline-junkie pasts for a tough subsistence lifestyle as they also deal with the challenges associated with growing old. He joins the brothers as they go cattle-wrangling, rock climbing and skydiving, while Ben also discovers more about them and why they decided to cut themselves off from civilisation. Once parachute instructors, police informants and bounty hunters, they are now organic farmers who are preparing for doomsday.

p.t: Rivalry in Music – Furtwängler vs. Toscanini
p.d: Two men without whom the profession of conductor would not be what it is today. Two men who couldn't be more different from each other: Arturo Toscanini and Wilhelm Furtwängler. The former was rigorously faithful to the musical score, the latter conducted with radical subjectivity. In 1931 they both conducted at the Bayreuth Festival – for the first and last time. Soon the polite rivalry turned into bitter enmity. Both men were forced to take a stand on the regimes in their respective countries – and chose radically different paths. Toscanini, the dictator, bravely challenged Mussolini; Furtwängler, a conservative, meanwhile proclaimed that art is always apolitical and reluctantly made a pact with the Nazis. The documentary not only opens up the different musical universes of the two great conductors by retracing their careers in Milan, Bayreuth and New York, but also raises a question that is more topical than ever: what has art to do with politics?Subtitles available for this program with your remote control

The Torrevieja Euromarina Optimist International Trophy is a scoring regatta for the Optimist Excellence Cup, the international event that this year has achieved a record participation with 406 sailors from 27 countries. High level sailing meets in Torrevieja, which hosts the third round of the Optimist Excellence Cup (OEC) 2021-2022 after its previous stops in Vigo and El Puerto de Santa María. With four days of competition and a total of 12 races planned, we can expect an excellent competition to unwind in Torrevieja, Spain. After previous cancelations due to COVID, this season is filled with excitement and action in the four regattas that conform the OEC. With its international scope, it drives the attention of sailors worldwide for a record attendance. Enjoy the competition in Torrevieja for the Euromarina Optimist International Trophy.

The island of Ugljan, right across the town of Zadar, is known for its olives and olive produce. Beautiful sandy beaches and crystal clear sea will take your breath away. Small islands of Zadar archipelago are very popular for sailing and we will show you why. The town of Zadar was founded in Roman times and by every step through it you will stumble upon amazing heritage from the ancient times. Of course, we couldn't resist and we visited crazy funny Museum of Illusions.

Hyvällä ryhdillä on mukava lähteä kohti päivän askareita. Jumppa on mahdollista toteuttaa istuen ja seisten, eli jokainen voi tulla mukaan.

Rauhalliset ja lempeät liikkeet auttavat sinua rauhoittumaan ja antamaan erityistä huomiota juuri sille, mitä kehosi tarvitsee. Aivojumpan avulla saadaan treeniä aivoille, mikä onkin yhtä tärkeää, kuin kehon harjoittaminen. Harjoitus sopii kaikille.

Siinä samassa seitsemän- ja kymmenvuotiaat pojat päättävät suunnata Amerikkaan Teräsmiehen luo ja pyytää supersankaria rankaisemaan kaikkia, jotka ovat olleet ilkeitä veljeksille. Listan kärjessä komeilee itse Saddam. Vaikka pojilla ei ole passeja, rahaa eikä kulkuvälinettä, he lähtevät rohkeasti tavoittelemaan unelmaansa.

Vähitellen Oskarille selviää, että Eli on vampyyri, jonka on juotava toisten verta selviytyäkseen. Oskarin on päätettävä mitä hän on valmis hyväksymään...

Carl Hamilton onnistuu soluttautumaan kansainväliseen rikollisjärjestöön, joka on varastanut edistyneitä ruotsalaisia GPS-ohjattuja panssarintorjuntaohjuksia, mutta järjestön kimppuun iskee äkkiä kuolettavasti hyvin koulutettu palkkasoturijoukko, jonka työnantajasta ei ole tietoa. Hamilton selviää verilöylystä hengissä, mutta ohjukset katoavat jäljettömiin, kunnes rauhaa ajava somalialainen poliitikko joutuu iskun kohteeksi. Lisäksi ruotsalaisen aseteknikon sieppaus saa Ruotsin pääministerin palkkaamaan yksityisen turvallisuusyhtiön pelastusyritystä varten – sillä ehdolla, että mukaan pääsee myös ruotsalainen tarkkailija, nimittäin Carl Hamilton. Hamilton tajuaa, että hänen vuotensa salaisena agenttina ovat tehneet hänestä tappokoneen, ja hän haluaa jättää sen taakseen. Hän on tavannut naisen ja toivoo elämänsä tulleen käännekohtaan, mutta aikana, jona korruptoituneet poliitikot ja sodista rahallisesti hyötyvät tahot uhkaavat maailmanrauhaa, hän tajuaa pian, ettei se ole mahdollista. Vaarallinen tehtävä vie Hamiltonin Somalian karusta erämaasta Beirutin kaduille ja Tukholman saaristoon. Nyt Carl Hamiltonin täytyy toimia parhaansa mukaan kansakunnan puolesta.

Karlssonin veljekset ovat kaksosia, mutta eivät tiedä toistensa olemassaolosta. Yksi on menestynyt ja tarkka lakimies Tukholmassa ja toinen vetelä vilunki pohjoisesta. Veljekset kohtaavat toisensa perunkirjoituksessa, ja seuraukset mullistavat molempien elämän.
